title: Direct mapping of the temperature and velocity gradients in discs. Imaging the vertical CO snow line around IM Lupi
question: Can the altitude, velocity and temperature of the CO emitting layers of the IM Lupi disc be measured directly from ALMA channel maps, locating the vertical CO snow line?

recipe.method: CASA calibration, self-calibration on continuum applied to lines, CLEAN with manual masks, with and without uvcontsub

recipe.goal: Locate emission maxima along isovelocity curves and derive r, h
recipe.method: In each channel map, for x sampled every 0.08", find near/far-side maxima y_n,y_f; y_c=(y_f+y_n)/2; r from ellipse geometry; h=(y_c-y_star)/sin i
key_parameters: x sampled every 0.08" (~1/4 beam); star at continuum peak
assumptions: Circular Keplerian orbits parallel to midplane; inclination 48 deg; no radial or vertical flows

recipe.method: v=(v_obs-v_syst) r/((x-x_star) sin i); compare with altitude-dependent Keplerian and pressure-gradient terms
assumptions: Central mass 1 Msun (PV fit), distance 161 pc

recipe.method: Peak brightness temperature of optically thick 12CO and 13CO taken as kinetic temperature (LTE); central 12CO channels within ±0.7 km/s excluded

recipe.goal: Illustrative MCFOST model of CO depletion
recipe.method: MCFOST radiative transfer with simple CO chemistry, parameters fitted by genetic algorithm on Band 6 channel maps; test depletion scenarios
key_parameters: Freezeout at T<21 K with factor epsilon=8e-5
assumptions: Gas temperature equals dust temperature; CO in LTE

recipe.method: Deconvolve major-axis profile, convert to surface density, iterate MCFOST until profile changes <1%

evidence.quote: At a distance of 200 au, the $^{12}$CO emission originates from an altitude of $\approx$65 au, while the $^{13}$CO originates from $\approx$25 au.

answer_key.quantity: Power-law exponent of 12CO layer altitude (r<300 au)

evidence.quote: power-law exponent of 1.8$\pm$0.2 and 2.1$\pm$0.4 for the altitude of $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO

answer_key.quantity: Power-law exponent of 13CO layer altitude (r<300 au)

evidence.loc: 4.4 Two-dimensional temperature structure and vertical CO snow line
evidence.quote: the $^{12}$CO temperature is virtually constant at $\approx$ 21 K, between 130 and 300 au

answer_key.quantity: Temperature at 400 au above snow line

evidence.loc: 4.4 Two-dimensional temperature structure and vertical CO snow line

answer_key.quantity: Deviation from altitude-dependent Keplerian at 400 au

evidence.loc: 4.3 Vertical velocity gradient and sub-Keplerian rotation
evidence.quote: the measured deviations from the altitude dependent Keplerian rotation are of the order of $0.15$ km/s

answer_key.quantity: Maximum continuum optical depth outside 100 au

score_reason: Public data and clear geometric method, but imaging parameters, code and uncertainty estimation are not given.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, geometric method fully described by equations, numeric results (21 K plateau, altitudes, exponents).
